articles.title: US Firm Reflect Orbital Buys Two Skyroot Launches After Vikram-1 Success
articles.excerpt: California-based Reflect Orbital has purchased two dedicated launches from India's Skyroot Aerospace — one on Vikram-1 and one on the in-development Vikram-1U — months after Vikram-1 became India's first privately developed rocket to reach orbit on its maiden flight.
articles.image_caption: Skyroot's Vikram-1 rocket on the launch pad. US firm Reflect Orbital has bought two launches from the Hyderabad startup after the Vikram-1 success.
articles.nri_angle: A US company buying dedicated launches from Hyderabad-based Skyroot is a landmark export win for India's private space sector, built by former ISRO engineers and watched closely by the diaspora's large space and engineering community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Vikram-S launched, first Indian private rocket.
Vikram-1 achieves orbit on maiden flight.
Skyroot valued at $1.1 billion, becomes unicorn.

articles.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Says He Would Cut Off Customers Building Unsafe AI
articles.excerpt: In a London interview, Nvidia's chief executive said he would halt chip supplies to a developer building unsafe AI — after talks first — while arguing that current safety fears are overstated and backing UK safety research with $250 million in computing resources.
articles.image_caption: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang speaks in front of an Nvidia backdrop. Huang told Bloomberg in London that he would halt chip supplies to a customer developing unsafe AI software, after a conversation first.
articles.nri_angle: Nvidia's stance on safety conditions for chip access, and its $250 million UK compute commitment for safety research, directly affect the Indian engineers, researchers and founders who build on Nvidia hardware in the US, UK and India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Play Opens a Private Lane for AI-Built Personal Android Apps
articles.excerpt: US users aged 18 and over can now build an app in Google AI Studio and run it on their own phone through Google Play — no developer account, no public listing, and no $25 registration fee.
articles.nri_angle: US-based Indian developers and hobbyists get the feature first; Google has given no India launch date, so India-based builders must wait or use a US account.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: LSEG Partners With Nvidia to Analyse Decades of Market Data in Seconds
articles.excerpt: Using Nvidia GPU-accelerated computing, LSEG says years of Tick History — 110 trillion rows across 100 million instruments — can be analysed in seconds instead of hours, without copying the dataset.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin quants, traders and data engineers in global finance hubs are among the users who would run intraday back-tests on LSEG data if their firms adopt the GPU pipeline.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Space Startups Raise Record $20.8 Billion as Infrastructure Bets Surge
articles.excerpt: Seraphim's third-quarter report shows funding nearly tripled from the prior quarter across a record 216 deals, led by launch and space-access companies.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers and founders in the global space sector face a funding market rewarding infrastructure ventures with proven commercial and government demand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Infosys AI Services Could Be Nearly Half Its Work in 2-3 Years, CEO Salil Parekh Says
articles.excerpt: AI services were over 8% of Infosys revenue last quarter and are growing at a double-digit rate sequentially, Parekh told the Bloomberg New Economy Forum. About 80,000 of its roughly 300,000 employees already use coding tools.
articles.image_caption: The Infosys name is displayed on the facade of an Infosys office building. CEO Salil Parekh said AI services could account for nearly half of the company's work within two to three years.
articles.nri_angle: Infosys is one of the largest employers of Indian technology professionals worldwide; a shift of half its delivery work to AI services reshapes what skills its US and India workforces are hired and trained for.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Developer Who Cloned Photoshop With AI Now Builds Word, Excel and PowerPoint Replicas
articles.excerpt: Brandon Thomas's WordCraft, GridCraft and DeckCraft are free, open-source Rust replicas built with Claude - impressive in scope, but still alpha software at roughly half to three-fifths real-work readiness.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora professionals who rely on Office get a free, cross-platform alternative to test on copies of files, with clear parity figures showing why it is not yet a replacement for critical work.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anthropic to Open Its Books to Investors as AI Lab Financials Drive the Tech Trade
articles.excerpt: The Claude developer will present third-quarter figures to institutional investors this week, with a confidential SEC filing already in and a possible listing ahead.
articles.nri_angle: Anthropic's valuation will benchmark the AI-lab business that Indian IT firms such as HCLTech are building partnerships around.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS Says Eighty Percent of New Hires Will Bring AI Skills
articles.excerpt: India's largest IT services company says four in five new hires will have digital and AI skills, after AI-led work reached 10% of September-quarter revenue.
articles.image_caption: A Tata Consultancy Services office. TCS said 80 percent of its new hires will bring AI skills.
articles.nri_angle: TCS hiring rules shape entry routes for Indian engineers at home and abroad, so its AI-first filter changes what diaspora families should expect from a first IT job.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Balisto's Electric Farm Machine Targets India's Labour Shortage for Small Farmers
articles.excerpt: Mumbai-based Balisto Agritech's 130 Pro combines weeding, rotavating and trolley work in one electric unit priced from Rs 2.5 lakh, as the Tech30 startup tries to scale beyond its first 30 customers.
articles.image_caption: An electric tractor in a field (file photo). Balisto's electric farm machine targets India's labour shortage for small farmers.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora readers with family farms in India, a single electric machine that cuts diesel and hired-labour dependence speaks directly to a cost pressure felt in many households.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

Both worked at Boston Consulting Group

articles.title: Apple's Diwali AirPods 5 Brings a Rangoli-Engraved Case to India at Rs 17,900
articles.excerpt: The India-exclusive special edition costs the same as the standard model, is capped at two pairs per customer, and anchors a festive campaign that includes free rangoli workshops in the US, Canada, Malaysia and Singapore.
articles.image_caption: Apple's special-edition AirPods 5 case carries a rangoli-inspired engraving around a heart-eyes emoji, also printed on the box. The Diwali edition is an India exclusive priced at Rs 17,900.
articles.nri_angle: The earbuds are India-only, but Apple's rangoli workshops run in the US, Canada, Malaysia and Singapore — the diaspora-facing half of the Diwali campaign.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Zoho Skips Annual Pay Hikes as AI Costs Surge, Vembu Warns on Software Jobs
articles.excerpt: Sridhar Vembu blamed a fourfold jump in server prices and rising AI usage costs, said headcount has been flat for 18 months, and apologised to employees — while vowing to avoid mass layoffs.
articles.image_caption: Zoho headquarters in Chennai. Zoho skipped annual pay hikes as AI infrastructure costs surge, and founder Sridhar Vembu warned on software jobs.
articles.nri_angle: Even a profitable, bootstrapped software major is diverting pay and hiring money into AI infrastructure — the same trade-off now facing Indian engineers in India and abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Lattice Launches Quantum-Resistant Security Stack for AI Data Centres
articles.excerpt: Lattice Sentry 5.0 adds post-quantum cryptography to firmware protection and attestation for AI infrastructure, pairing Lattice FPGAs with AMI software in a CNSA 2.0-aligned package.
articles.image_caption: A data centre server hall. Lattice Semiconductor launched its Sentry 5.0 quantum-resistant security stack for AI data centres.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian and diaspora engineers building cloud and AI infrastructure in the US, Sentry's adoption by server makers will signal how quickly quantum-resistant firmware becomes a standard purchasing requirement.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: Includes secure firmware updates and anti-rollback protection

items.event: OCP Global Summit in San Jose

articles.title: How to Use Google Gemini Spark to Automate Everyday Tasks
articles.excerpt: Google's Spark agent can summarise email, log leads and work across Workspace apps in the background. Here is who can use it, how to set up a task, and where to keep a human check.
articles.image_caption: Google Gemini, whose Spark background agent can automate everyday tasks across Gmail, Docs, Calendar and Drive for paid users.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora professionals balancing work, family calendars and paperwork across time zones, Spark offers a practical way to automate routine email and document chores without handing over sensitive details.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

steps.detail: You need a Google AI Pro or Ultra plan, Keep activity switched on, and to be outside the EEA, Switzerland, the UK and Nigeria.
In the Gemini mobile, Mac or web app, select Menu, then Spark.
State what triggers the job, what to extract or create, and where the result should go, in plain language.
Upload a file, or attach one from Drive or a notebook, before submitting.

steps.step: Submit and watch the first runs
steps.detail: Tap or click Submit, then review progress under Menu, Spark, then Tasks.

steps.step: Turn a repeat job into a skill
steps.detail: Save the routine as a skill and reuse it by typing a slash followed by the skill name in a later prompt.

articles.title: Microsoft Unveils Maia 300, Plans Multi-Gigawatt Rollout of Its Own AI Chips From 2027
articles.excerpt: Maia will become the primary inference system for Copilot, Teams and GitHub, as Microsoft moves to cut the cost of running AI on Nvidia hardware. Nadella called it the company's biggest bet yet on its own silicon.
articles.nri_angle: Cheaper Azure inference changes the economics for Indian IT services firms and startups building AI products on Microsoft's cloud.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Maia 200 in production across US, Europe, Australia
GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Foundry workloads move to Maia 200

articles.title: Bay Area Startup Tavus Says Its AI Avatar Fooled 48% in a Job Interview Test
articles.excerpt: In Tavus's own test, 26 of 54 participants thought the Griffin avatar interviewer was human — and were 79% confident. The result has not been independently verified.
articles.image_caption: A video interview conducted on a laptop screen. Tavus says its Griffin AI avatar was mistaken for a human interviewer by 48% of participants in its job-interview test.
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals in US tech hiring pass through heavy screening pipelines; first-round video interviews are increasingly synthetic, and candidates can ask whether the interviewer is human.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: HCLTech Signs Anthropic Pact, Will Build Dedicated Agentic AI Business Unit
articles.excerpt: India's third-largest IT services firm will set up a centre of excellence to build enterprise AI-agent solutions around Claude, Cowork and Claude Code, with safety and governance as stated priorities.
articles.nri_angle: The deal signals where Indian IT's centre of gravity is moving: from labour-arbitrage outsourcing toward building and governing enterprise AI agents — the work Indian engineers in India and abroad will increasingly be hired to do.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.label: Key Focus Areas: Safety, Cybersecurity, Governance

articles.title: Microsoft's Brad Smith says AI needs global rules: less oversight than milk
articles.excerpt: In a BBC interview, Microsoft's president urged mandatory emergency brakes, incident reports and independent evaluation of AI systems — and said Britain's AI Security Institute is best placed to lead.
articles.image_caption: Microsoft president Brad Smith, who has called for global AI rules with mandatory emergency brakes.
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers and founders across the AI supply chain face a costly regulatory patchwork; a UK-led global standard would directly shape how their products ship worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Software developer job postings are rising — but only at the top
articles.excerpt: U.S. software job postings are up nearly 15% since early 2025 even as AI agents write more code — because the rebound is concentrated in senior and AI-focused roles, while the entry-level pipeline keeps thinning.
articles.image_caption: Software development work. US job postings have risen 15% since February 2025 but remain below pre-pandemic levels.
articles.nri_angle: The split favors experienced engineers — Indian tech workers in the U.S. and India should steer toward senior-track, AI-supervised development skills rather than competing for junior boilerplate roles the models now cover.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DeepMind's Lila Ibrahim: what young engineers must do to survive AI
articles.excerpt: Google DeepMind's chief AI readiness officer told NDTV that entry-level engineering jobs are drying up as automation takes over routine coding — and the survivors will be the ones who can point to what is irreducibly human in their work.
articles.image_caption: Lila Ibrahim, chief operating officer of Google DeepMind
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers face the sharpest version of this squeeze — 37% of entry-level tasks already handled or augmented by AI, with fresher campus hiring in multi-year decline.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.label: Entry-level tasks handled by AI in India

articles.title: TCS CEO Says Traditional IT Growth Will Taper as AI Revenue Crosses $3 Billion
articles.excerpt: K. Krithivasan's BusinessLine interview puts a number on the pivot — $3 billion in annualized AI revenue, up 19% in a quarter — as the old services model slows.
articles.image_caption: TCS chief executive K. Krithivasan. He told The Hindu BusinessLine that traditional IT services growth will taper as clients shift spending to AI.
articles.nri_angle: TCS employs lakhs of Indians in the US on H-1Bs and green-card queues and was just suspended from the PERM programme; its AI pivot defines what skills keep Indian tech workers employable.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.card_title: Impact of AI on Traditional IT

articles.title: Automation Could Shrink US Labor Demand by 36 Million Jobs by 2035, McKinsey Warns
articles.excerpt: The McKinsey Global Institute says 11 million US workers — 7% of the workforce — may need entirely new occupations as AI adoption accelerates, in "the largest workforce transformation in US history."
articles.image_caption: An industrial robot at work (file photo) — a McKinsey Global Institute report warns automation could shrink US labor demand by the equivalent of 36 million jobs by 2035.
articles.nri_angle: Indian tech workers in the US face 70% automation adoption of current work hours by 2035; reskilling toward growing fields like healthcare, construction and management is the actionable hedge.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Semiconductor Market to Hit $200 Billion by 2035 as Five Plants Go Live: EY-IESA
articles.excerpt: The EY-IESA report unveiled at SEMICON India 2026 projects threefold growth as commercial chip production begins at five units, including new lines at Mohali and Surat.
articles.image_caption: Officials launch the EY-IESA report Semicon India 2.0 at SEMICON India 2026 in New Delhi. The report projects India semiconductor market will grow from nearly $64 billion in 2026 to $200 billion by 2035.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian engineers in the US chip industry, the $200 billion projection maps where design centres, fab projects and supply-chain careers will grow over the next decade.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Zomato Founder Deepinder Goyal's 'Temple' Wearable Tracks Brain Blood Flow, Priced Around ₹75,000
articles.excerpt: The pill-shaped device, worn between the forehead and the ear, uses optical sensing to track cerebral blood flow; waitlist pre-orders open soon ahead of shipments before end-2026.
articles.image_caption: The gold-coloured Temple wearable worn between the forehead and the ear. The pill-shaped device tracks cerebral blood flow through its BrainFlow optical sensing system.
articles.nri_angle: For health-conscious NRIs tracking the next wave of Indian-built health tech, Temple is the most ambitious wearable to come out of India — but at ₹75,000-plus and with peer review pending, the waitlist is where the smart money waits.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Curiosity Captures Martian Sunrise Mirroring Arizona's Monument Valley
articles.excerpt: NASA's rover photographed wind-carved yardang cliffs at dawn on Mount Sharp — an orange sky, blue sunrise tones, and a three-billion-year geological puzzle.
articles.image_caption: NASA's Curiosity rover on Mars. Its latest images captured a sunrise that looks strikingly like Arizona's Monument Valley.
articles.nri_angle: Curiosity's imagery resonates strongly with Indian-origin science enthusiasts as ISRO's Chandrayaan and Gaganyaan programs make planetary exploration a point of diaspora pride.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Infosys Sees No Material Impact From US Suspension of PERM Program
articles.excerpt: India's second-largest IT firm told stock exchanges on Saturday that the Labor Department's freeze on green-card labor certifications would not affect it materially, even as the suspension stalls thousands of immigrant worker cases across eight tech companies.
articles.image_caption: The Infosys campus in Bengaluru. The U.S. Department of Labor suspended eight firms, including Infosys, from the PERM green-card labor program on Oct. 8, 2026; Infosys said on Oct. 10 that it does not expect a material impact.
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals face the longest green-card backlogs, so the freeze hits H-1B professionals at the eight suspended firms hardest — the six-year H-1B extension clock cannot start without a PERM filing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Mobile Congress 2026 Closes With Agri-AI, 5G Automation and Rural Push
articles.excerpt: The 10th edition of the telecom flagship ended Saturday with agriculture AI, autonomous 5G agents and rural connectivity as the closing-day themes.
articles.image_caption: A view from the India Mobile Congress 2026. The 10th edition of the telecom flagship concluded on Saturday with a focus on agricultural AI, 5G automation and rural connectivity.
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora's tech professionals and investors, IMC 2026's agri-AI focus signals where India's next deep-tech opportunity sits — at the intersection of telecom infrastructure, AI and agriculture.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Space Startups Go Global as Defence Demand Surges Past ISRO's Shadow
articles.excerpt: From a single company in 2014 to 440 startups today, India's private space sector is chasing defence contracts and lunar technology — with China firmly in its sights.
articles.image_caption: The Vikram-S rocket launch by Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace — India's first private-sector rocket launch, in 2022
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora's engineers and investors, the space startup boom is one of the clearest on-ramps for NRI capital and talent into India's deep-tech economy — with $618.5 million in private investment and foreign government contracts already flowing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Weta CTO: AI Tools Bring Efficiency, But Tech Must Partner With Creatives
articles.excerpt: Kimball Thurston told Netflix's Creative Asia panel at Busan that AI is delivering real production gains — and that tech companies should collaborate more with the artists using it.
articles.image_caption: A Gollum statue at Wellington Airport; Gollum was created by Weta Digital for The Lord of the Rings
articles.nri_angle: Thousands of Indian animators and VFX artists work on global pipelines — including for studios like Weta — so this debate over AI tools versus artist control directly affects diaspora creative careers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NASA's New Moon Missions Will Hunt Lunar Caves, Ice, and Hidden Hazards
articles.excerpt: Three new PRISM investigations will scout underground shelters, map hidden ice, and monitor environmental hazards — the reconnaissance for humanity's first permanent lunar outpost.
articles.image_caption: An artist’s concept of astronauts working at a future lunar base. NASA has selected three new science investigations to scout shelters, ice, and hazards for a permanent Moon outpost.
articles.nri_angle: India, an Artemis Accords signatory with its own lunar ambitions through ISRO's Chandrayaan program, is a natural partner in the Moon Base era — and NASA's open science selections set the research agenda Indian planetary scientists will build on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple's LG Smart-Home Gear Gets Exclusive iPhone Proximity Feature
articles.excerpt: Code found in iOS 27 shows iPhones will detect Apple's co-developed LG accessories on tap, popping a Dynamic Island hint for instant controls — as Apple stages a "Welcome home" event on October 13.
articles.image_caption: The Apple Home app icon from iOS 27. Apple is staging a HomeKit reboot with LG-built accessories, ahead of its "Welcome home" event on October 13, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: LG is already a trusted household brand in India, so Apple-ecosystem users in India and among NRIs get a familiar name on the accessories — even if iPhone-exclusive perks keep the lineup an Apple-first buy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Expected launch of LG smart-home devices

articles.title: Google Unveils Gemini Agent for Work as Enterprise AI Race Heats Up
articles.excerpt: At its "Gemini at Work 2026" event, Google Cloud introduced a single AI agent that works inside Workspace, Microsoft 365 and Slack, routing each task to the best model — Google's Gemini or Anthropic's Claude.
articles.image_caption: Google's Gemini app; Google Cloud unveiled a "Gemini agent" for work on October 8 (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The enterprise agent race matters for Indian IT services professionals and global capability centers, whose daily work runs inside Workspace and Slack — whoever wins this layer sets the workflow standards and reskilling agenda for them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Pikachu Plush Spent 67 Days Aboard the International Space Station
articles.excerpt: The ESA–Pokémon partnership for World Space Week sent a spacesuited plush into orbit with astronaut Sophie Adenot; 1,040 orbits later, the tour video is out.
articles.image_caption: A Pikachu plush in a custom spacesuit floats inside the International Space Station's Cupola observatory. The toy spent 67 days aboard the station as part of an ESA-Pokémon partnership marking World Space Week.
articles.nri_angle: The ISS crew includes Indian-origin NASA astronaut Anil Menon on Expedition 75 — and ESA's Pikachu partnership shows how space agencies are reaching the next generation of young space fans, including in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Manus Raises Over $500 Million in First Round Since Meta Breakup
articles.excerpt: Butterfly Effect's AI agent startup, unwound from Meta's $2 billion-plus acquisition by Beijing in April, now has fresh capital and a reported $500 million revenue run rate.
articles.image_caption: The Manus logo displayed on a screen. The AI agent startup raised more than $500 million in its first funding round since unwinding Meta's $2 billion-plus acquisition.
articles.nri_angle: The Manus raise signals accelerating commercial demand for AI agents — the same enterprise AI wave that India's IT services firms and 2,000+ global capability centres are racing to serve.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nvidia-Backed Firmus Scraps Landmark $5 Billion IPO, Blaming Market Volatility
articles.excerpt: The AI data-center builder withdrew its ASX listing — set to be Australia's biggest since Telstra — after investors balked at a $44 billion valuation; it will raise private capital instead.
articles.image_caption: Server racks and monitoring displays inside a data center. Firmus, which builds AI data centers, withdrew its landmark Australian listing on October 9, citing market volatility.
articles.nri_angle: A landmark AI-infrastructure IPO collapse that signals how selectively markets are now pricing the AI boom — relevant context for tech investors and professionals worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jio's 1,600-Satellite Plan Gets Green Light as Starlink's India Launch Stalls
articles.excerpt: IN-SPACe has cleared Reliance Jio's low-Earth-orbit constellation as technically sound, while Starlink, JioSatcom and Eutelsat OneWeb await Home Ministry security clearances before switching on commercial services.
articles.image_caption: Elon Musk appears in a graphic showing Starlink satellites over India. Starlink has secured a satcom licence and IN-SPACe authorisation, but commercial services await a pending Home Ministry security clearance.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs with family in India's remote regions, Jio's sovereign constellation promises affordable rural broadband — and SpaceX-style competition could cut the cost of staying connected.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.card_title: Projected Timeline for Jio's Satellite Services

articles.title: OpenAI Bans Russian and Iranian Networks Using ChatGPT for Influence Campaigns
articles.excerpt: The company says the Russian 'Dark Clark' operation was the most sophisticated front-identity campaign it has disrupted, while Iran's 'Bogus Bylines' placed nearly 100 articles in real outlets under fake journalist personas.
articles.image_caption: A silhouetted figure works at a bank of monitors in a dark operations room. OpenAI says Russian and Iranian operatives used ChatGPT to draft reports and content for covert influence campaigns targeting Latin America and other regions.
articles.nri_angle: One Russian front posed as a platform covering the Indian diaspora in Latin America — evidence that diaspora communities are prime targets for influence operations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Navya Naveli Nanda Launches Naveli Ventures to Back India's Deep-Tech Ambitions
articles.excerpt: The Nanda Family Office's venture arm will invest across deep-tech, space, AI, clean energy, advanced manufacturing and health — formalising a strategy three years in the making.
articles.image_caption: Navya Naveli Nanda photographed in Mumbai. The entrepreneur formally launched Naveli Ventures, the Nanda Family Offices venture arm, on October 6, 2026, to back deep-tech and frontier-technology startups.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin deep-tech founders in the US often struggle to raise from Indian capital; a serious Naveli Ventures becomes another bridge between Silicon Valley's Indian founders and Mumbai's family money.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cal AI's 19-Year-Old Founder Raises $10M for New AI Startup Persona
articles.excerpt: Zach Yadegari, whose calorie-tracking app was acquired by MyFitnessPal, raised $10 million led by Vine Ventures for Persona — an AI assistant starting in iMessage and moving to a $179 wristband.
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora's large contingent of tech founders and engineers, Persona is one to watch — a second act from a teenager who already built one of the fastest-growing consumer AI apps of the decade.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google's New AI Note-Taking App Transcribes Meetings Entirely Offline
articles.excerpt: AI Edge Foresight, an experimental Mac app built on EmbeddingGemma 2 and Gemma 4, keeps all audio and files on-device — a privacy pitch aimed at confidential meetings.
articles.image_caption: Google's AI Edge Foresight app transcribes meetings entirely offline on Apple Silicon Macs, with no cloud subscription required. (Pictured: Googleplex headquarters in Mountain View.)
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora's large contingent of tech workers handling confidential work, on-device transcription is a genuine privacy upgrade — but the app is experimental and English-first for now.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.card_title: Key Features of AI Edge Foresight

articles.title: Meta Deploys AI to Catch Ads That Secretly Funnel Users to Child Abuse Material
articles.excerpt: The company's new tools target "signposting" ads that look benign but route users to illegal material off-platform — and Meta says it actioned 5.3 million exploitation items in India this half-year.
articles.image_caption: A Meta logo displayed on a wall. The company said it actioned 33.2 million pieces of child sexual exploitation content on Facebook and Instagram in the first half of 2026.
articles.nri_angle: India accounts for roughly 16% of Meta's global child-exploitation takedowns, making this directly relevant to diaspora families whose children use Instagram and Facebook — and to relatives back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India to Release AI Regulation Consultation Paper Within a Month, Vaishnaw Says
articles.excerpt: IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced the consultation paper will cover AI safety, deepfakes, and the technology's psychological impact — with industry expected to carry the main burden of compliance.
articles.image_caption: Union IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw. India will release its AI regulation consultation paper within a month, he said.
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers, product leaders, and AI startups abroad will face new compliance duties for the Indian market, from content labeling to takedown timelines, once this consultation becomes law.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

Amended IT Rules notified targeting synthetic content

articles.title: UPI Merchant Fee Rollout May Be Deferred to January 2027 Amid Retailer Pushback
articles.excerpt: Less than a week before the 0.40% UPI merchant fee was due to begin, retailers and fintech firms are pressing NPCI to delay it until January 2027 — and a decision is expected within days.
articles.image_caption: A UPI payment being made via a smartphone QR code scan. India may defer the proposed 0.40% merchant discount rate on UPI payments above ₹2,000 from October 15, 2026 to January 1, 2027 after pushback from retailer associations.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs using UPI during visits to India or through its international acceptance pay nothing under the framework, since the fee falls on Indian merchants — but the fight over who funds UPI’s next phase shapes the system’s sustainability as it goes global.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.card_title: Impact of UPI Fee on Merchants

articles.title: India Targets One Billion 5G Users by 2030 as Scindia Opens IMC 2026
articles.excerpt: Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia told the 10th India Mobile Congress that India has 550 million 5G users — the fastest adoption anywhere in the world — and set a goal of one billion by 2030, alongside a resolve to lead the world on 6G.
articles.image_caption: Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia addresses an audience at a podium. Scindia on Thursday set a target of one billion 5G users by 2030 while inaugurating the 10th India Mobile Congress in New Delhi.
articles.nri_angle: India's 5G and 6G push is a career and investment signal for the diaspora's large telecom and AI workforce, while Modi's anti-fraud framework push addresses the cross-border scam calls diaspora families receive.

articles.title: Trump to Award Top Science Medals to Musk, Nadella, Dell at Summit
articles.excerpt: The president will present the National Medals of Science and Technology and Innovation at Thursday's White House 'Science: A New Golden Age Summit' — the first time he has awarded either honor.
articles.image_caption: President Donald Trump embraces Elon Musk during a public appearance. Trump is set to award Musk the National Medal of Science at Thursday's White House summit.
articles.nri_angle: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, born in Hyderabad, will receive the National Medal of Technology and Innovation — a rare White House-level honor for an Indian-born tech leader.

articles.title: ChatGPT's Teen Safety Guardrails Fail in Crisis, Independent Testing Finds
articles.excerpt: Common Sense Media's Youth AI Safety Institute ran more than 4,000 test prompts on teen accounts and rated ChatGPT for Teens an "unacceptable risk" for under-18s, urging OpenAI to restrict the chatbot to adults until its safeguards are independently verified.
articles.image_caption: A smartphone showing the ChatGPT app next to a laptop. Independent testing found the chatbot's teen safety guardrails failed in crisis scenarios.
articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora families are among the heaviest adopters of AI tools for teens' schoolwork, so the finding that ChatGPT for Teens' parental alerts and study safeguards fail in practice is a direct, practical warning for parents — not abstract policy news.

articles.title: Teaching AI to Act Drunk Makes It Leak Secrets, UNSW Study Finds
articles.excerpt: Three Indian-origin researchers showed that training or prompting five popular AI models to imitate drunken behavior made them far easier to jailbreak and more willing to disclose confidential information.
articles.image_caption: An illustration of a robot sitting at a bar counter with a wine bottle and a glass of amber liquid. UNSW researchers found that AI models prompted or trained to imitate drunken behavior become easier to jailbreak and more likely to leak information they were told to keep confidential.
articles.nri_angle: The research team — Anudeex Shetty, Aditya Joshi and Salil Kanhere — are Indian-origin researchers at UNSW whose work feeds directly into global AI safety practice.
